summary_paragraph: A 60-year-old woman with a history of mast cell degranulation syndrome, achalasia, and coronary artery disease s/p CABG was admitted after developing acute dyspnea, chest tightness, wheezing, and itching following an EGD with Botox injection. Despite premedication, she experienced a mast cell activation episode and was transferred from the procedure site to the ED. She responded well to her standard treatment protocol with Benadryl, Solumedrol, albuterol, and oxygen. Chest imaging showed mild bibasilar atelectasis but no pneumonia or cardiac ischemia. Her symptoms resolved, and she remained stable overnight. She was discharged the following morning with instructions to resume chronic medications, follow up with her allergist and GI specialist, and use emergency measures if future reactions occur.
problems: Mast cell neoplasms of uncertain behavior
